audit_findings.title: Capitalized interest may defeat the stated after-interest owner-earnings treatment
audit_findings.magnitude: $74.750 million interest incurred, $51.364 million amortized to closings, and $23.386 million net capitalization in 2025
audit_findings.mechanism: An omitted increase in capitalized interest would overstate the $11.2 million OE anchor and every forecast and terminal value derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: We had no interest expense for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, as all interest incurred was capitalized to qualifying assets.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated omission. The filing shows that interest flowed through inventory and cost of closings, but the OE worksheet is absent. The $23.386 million increase in capitalized interest is more than twice the $11.2 million anchor, so failure to capture it exactly once could materially alter or eliminate positive anchor OE.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the 2025 OE calculation line by line to $74.750 million incurred, $51.364 million amortized, the $23.386 million inventory increase, and any directly expensed interest; then rerun all scenarios if the reconciliation identifies an omission or double count.

audit_findings.title: The bridge treats all cash as excess despite the business's operating-liquidity needs
audit_findings.magnitude: $807.267 million added, equal to 83.7% of the $965.0 million base equity value and $11.35 per diluted share; required operating cash unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash dollar for dollar even though some may fund inventory, land commitments, construction, interest, and routine liquidity already necessary to produce forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Our principal uses of cash include acquisition and development of land and lots, home construction, operating expenses, share repurchases and the payment of interest, routine liabilities, and dividends.
audit_findings.explanation: The full cash addition is demonstrated, while the amount that is genuinely excess is unresolved. Because cash supplies most of the stated equity value, even a moderate operating-cash reserve would materially reduce the $13.56 base value per share.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a June 30, 2026 sources-and-uses liquidity schedule covering seasonal construction needs, committed land funding, debt interest and maturities, minimum covenant headroom, and forecast reinvestment; add only the residual demonstrably excess cash and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Convertible-note dilution does not describe the same claim as the after-interest numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately 4.97 million excess denominator shares; removing them reduces the denominator from 71.146471 million to 66.180156 million and raises base value from $13.56 to approximately $14.58 per share, about 7.5%
audit_findings.mechanism: The denominator assumes full share conversion while OE retains note interest and the contract requires cash settlement of principal; this understates value per common share.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company is required to satisfy its conversion obligations by paying cash up to the principal amount of notes and settle any additional value in cash, shares of common stock or a combination of cash and shares of common stock, at the Company’s election.
audit_findings.explanation: The claim mismatch is demonstrated. At the valuation outputs, which are far below the $115.78 conversion price, treating the principal as converted equity is unsupported. Correcting only this mismatch raises base value by about $1.02 per share, but the resulting approximately $14.58 remains about 78% below the $67.33 market price, so it does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the denominator using cash-principal settlement and shares only for excess conversion value, net of capped-call protection; retain note interest in OE unless the numerator is also converted consistently.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor may be a community-cycle cash-flow snapshot rather than maintainable earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $11.2 million anchor versus the computed $210 million trend reference, a $198.8 million difference and an 18.75-fold ratio
audit_findings.mechanism: The latest-year OE anchor drives forecast OE, growth, operating present value, and terminal value; community-cycle working-capital timing can make one year's cash flow materially different from maintainable distributable earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash flows for each of our communities depend on their stage of the development cycle, and can differ substantially from reported earnings.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved normalization issue rather than a demonstrated arithmetic error. The filed disclosures confirm substantial timing differences between cash flow and earnings, while the OE series ranges from $11.2 million to $981.4 million. A full-cycle anchor could therefore move the operating valuation enough to alter the conclusion, and the existing too-hard flag does not resolve the numerical dependence on the $11.2 million snapshot.
audit_findings.action: Construct community-cycle OE using several complete cohorts or a normalized inventory-investment schedule, reconcile it to community count and lot-supply maintenance, and rerun the valuation with the supportable normalized anchor without changing the prescribed valuation method.

audit_findings.title: The purported share-count ceiling uses target PSU payout rather than a true maximum
audit_findings.mechanism: PSU payouts above target would increase fully diluted shares and reduce value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: The number of shares that may be issued to the award recipients may be greater or lesser than the target award amount depending on actual performance achieved as compared to the performance targets set forth in the awards.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that performance awards can settle above target, so the 1.006063 million target-based award allowance is not a true ceiling. The record does not disclose the applicable maximum payout percentages or the portion likely to earn above target, so incremental dilution and its materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the governing award agreements and 2026 proxy tables, calculate maximum shares by outstanding PSU tranche, reflect settlement and forfeiture terms, and rerun per-share values using both maximum and probability-weighted dilution.

audit_findings.title: A non-core purchased tax-credit gain may be embedded in the terminalized anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: no more than the computed $4.561 million difference between $10.161 million of total 2025 tax credits and $5.600 million of disclosed §45L credits; 40.7% of the $11.2 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: If included, the purchased-credit discount inflates anchor OE and is propagated through forecast OE and terminal value as though recurring.
audit_findings.evidence: During the fourth quarter of 2025, we entered into a tax credit transfer agreement to purchase 2025 §45Z alternative clean fuel production credits and we recognized a tax benefit representing the purchase discount between the credit value and the total purchase price.
audit_findings.explanation: Inclusion in OE remains unresolved, but the filing provides a usable upper bound: the §45Z benefit cannot exceed the $4.561 million residual tax-credit amount. Even removing that full bound and scaling the $157 million base operating value proportionally would reduce base equity value by about $64 million, or roughly $0.90 per share, leaving value near $12.66 versus the $67.33 market price. It therefore would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Identify the exact §45Z purchase discount and its cash-tax treatment, confirm whether it entered the $11.2 million OE anchor, and exclude it and its associated capital outlay consistently in a sensitivity rerun.
